The goals that Carol had made that day!

arxiv-2101-02331.title: Modeling and mitigation of cross-talk effects in readout noise with applications to the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
arxiv-2101-02331.creator: Filip B. Maciejewski, Flavio Baccari, Zoltán Zimborás, Michał Oszmaniec
arxiv-2101-02331.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Filip B. Maciejewski, Flavio Baccari, Zoltán Zimborás, Michał Oszmaniec. Measurement noise is one of the main sources of errors in currently available quantum devices based on superconducting qubits. At the same time, the complexity of its characterization and mitigation often exhibits exponential scaling with the system size. In this work, we introduce a correlated measurement noise model that can be efficiently described and characterized, and which admits effective noise-mitigation on the level of marginal probability distributions.

arxiv-2104-10614.title: On the Bogomolov-Gieseker inequality for tame Deligne-Mumford surfaces
arxiv-2104-10614.creator: Yunfeng Jiang and Promit Kundu
arxiv-2104-10614.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yunfeng Jiang and Promit Kundu. We generalize the Bogomolov-Gieseker inequality for semistable coherent sheaves on smooth projective surfaces to smooth Deligne-Mumford surfaces. We work over positive characteristic p > 0 p>0 and generalize Langer’s method to smooth Deligne-Mumford stacks.

arxiv-2107-00375.title: A Semiparametric Bayesian Approach to Epidemics,with Application to the Spread of the Coronavirus MERS in South Korea in 2015
arxiv-2107-00375.creator: Michael Schweinberger, Rashmi P. Bomiriya, Sergii Babkin
arxiv-2107-00375.description: Abstract We consider incomplete observations of stochastic processes governing the spread of infectious diseases through finite populations by way of contact. We propose a flexible semiparametric modeling framework with at least three advantages. First, it enables researchers to study the structure of a population contact network and its impact on the spread of infectious diseases.

arxiv-2109-03776.title: Potential model with bound-to-continuum approach for low-energy nucleon radiative capture by 12 C and 16 O
arxiv-2109-03776.creator: Nguyen Le Anh 1,2,3, Phan Nhut Huan 4,5, Bui Minh Loc 6,7
arxiv-2109-03776.description: Abstract The nucleon radiative capture reactions are important in pure and applied nuclear physics, especially in nuclear astrophysics. The keV-nucleon radiative capture reactions are studied with 12 C and 16 O targets using the bound-to-continuum potential model in which both scattering and bound states are treated simultaneously and based on the Skyrme Hartree-Fock approximation.

arxiv-2203-03760.title: Snow topography on undeformed Arctic sea ice captured by an idealized “snow dune” model
arxiv-2203-03760.creator: Predrag Popović, Justin Finkel, Mary C. Silber, Dorian S. Abbot
arxiv-2203-03760.description: Abstract Our ability to predict the future of Arctic sea ice is limited by ice’s sensitivity to detailed surface conditions such as the distribution of snow and melt ponds. Snow on top of the ice decreases ice’s thermal conductivity, increases its reflectivity (albedo), and provides a source of meltwater for melt ponds during summer that decrease the ice’s albedo.

arxiv-2204-02100.title: Self-supervised learning - A way to minimize time and effort for precision agriculture?
arxiv-2204-02100.creator: Michael L. Marszalek 1, Bertrand Le Saux 1, Pierre-Philippe Mathieu 1, Artur Nowakowski 2, Daniel Springer 3
arxiv-2204-02100.description: Abstract Machine learning, satellites or local sensors are key factors for a sustainable and resource-saving optimisation of agriculture and proved its values for the management of agricultural land. Up to now, the main focus was on the enlargement of data which were evaluated by means of supervised learning methods.

arxiv-2204-03608.title: Influence of light quark loops on the Wigner phase with Dyson-Schwinger equations approach
arxiv-2204-03608.creator: Jing-Hui Huang, Xiang-Yun Hu, Qi Wang, Xue-Ying Duan, Guang-Jun Wang, Huan Chen
arxiv-2204-03608.description: Abstract We study the influence of light quark loops on the Wigner phase by solving coupled Dyson-Schwinger equations for quark propagator and gluon propagator. We take the gluon propagator in the Nambu phase from N f N_{f} = 2 unquenched lattice QCD and choose various phenomenological models for the quark-gluon vertex.

arxiv-2305-15254.title: Pay Attention to Mean-Fields during Particle Cloud Generation
arxiv-2305-15254.creator: Benno Käch, Isabell-A. Melzer-Pellmann
arxiv-2305-15254.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Benno Käch, Isabell-A. Melzer-Pellmann. The generation of collider data using machine learning has emerged as a prominent research topic in particle physics due to the increasing computational challenges associated with traditional Monte Carlo simulation methods, particularly for future colliders with higher luminosity. Although generating particle clouds is analogous to generating point clouds, accurately modelling the complex correlations between the particles presents a considerable challenge. Additionally, variable particle cloud sizes further exacerbate these difficulties, necessitating more sophisticated models.

arxiv-2306-04941.title: A modified model for topic detection from a corpus and a new metric evaluating the understandability of topics
arxiv-2306-04941.creator: Tomoya Kitano, Yuto Miyatake, Daisuke Furihata
arxiv-2306-04941.description: Abstract This paper presents a modified neural model for topic detection from a corpus and proposes a new metric to evaluate the detected topics. The new model builds upon the embedded topic model incorporating some modifications such as document clustering. Numerical experiments suggest that the new model performs favourably regardless of the document’s length.

arxiv-2401-12380.creator: Michael Hagenow, Emmanuel Senft, Robert Radwin, Michael Gleicher, Michael Zinn, Bilge Mutlu
arxiv-2401-12380.description: Abstract . Many industrial tasks—such as sanding, installing fasteners, and wire harnessing—are difficult to automate due to task complexity and variability. We instead investigate deploying robots in an assistive role for these tasks, where the robot assumes the physical task burden and the skilled worker provides both the high-level task planning and low-level feedback necessary to effectively complete the task.

arxiv-2410-22327.title: Parametrised functor calculus: excision, spheres, and semiadditivity
arxiv-2410-22327.creator: Kaif Hilman, Sil Linskens
arxiv-2410-22327.description: Abstract We lay down the foundations of a theory of parametrised functor calculus , generalising parts of the functor calculus of Goodwillie. We introduce the notion of excisable posets and develop a theory of excisive approximations in this context. As an application, we introduce two different excisable posets when parametrising over an atomic orbital category.

arxiv-2412-15994.title: From discrete to continuum in the helical XY-model: emergence of chirality transitions in the S 1 S^{1} to S 2 S^{2} limit
arxiv-2412-15994.creator: Marco Cicalese, Dario Reggiani, Francesco Solombrino
arxiv-2412-15994.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Marco Cicalese, Dario Reggiani, Francesco Solombrino. We analyze the discrete-to-continuum limit of a frustrated ferromagnetic/anti-ferromagnetic 𝕊 2 \mathbb{S}^{2} -valued spin system on the lattice λ n ​ ℤ 2 \lambda_{n}\mathbb{Z}^{2} as λ n → 0 \lambda_{n}\to 0 . For 𝕊 2 \mathbb{S}^{2} spin systems close to the Landau-Lifschitz point (where the helimagnetic/ferromagnetic transition occurs), it is well established that for chirality transitions emerge with vanishing energy.

arxiv-2512-14251.title: An improved lower bound to Erdos’ problem concerning products of distances for fixed diameter
arxiv-2512-14251.creator: Nat Sothanaphan
arxiv-2512-14251.description: Abstract Erdos, Herzog and Piranian asked whether, for n n points in the plane with fixed diameter (maximum distance between points), an arrangement of a regular n n -gon maximizes their product of all pairs of distances. Recently, it was discovered that, for every even n ≥ 4 n\geq 4 , a regular n n -gon is not a maximizer.

arxiv-2602-08724.title: Rotated Lights for Consistent and Efficient 2D Gaussians Inverse Rendering
arxiv-2602-08724.creator: Geng Lin Matthias Zwicker
arxiv-2602-08724.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Geng Lin Matthias Zwicker. Inverse rendering aims to decompose a scene into its geometry, material properties and light conditions under a certain rendering model. It has wide applications like view synthesis, relighting, and scene editing. In recent years, inverse rendering methods have been inspired by view synthesis approaches like neural radiance fields and Gaussian splatting, which are capable of efficiently decomposing a scene into its geometry and radiance. They then further estimate the material and lighting that lead to the observed scene radiance.

britannica-1911-aerotherapeutics.title: Aerotherapeutics (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-aerotherapeutics.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-aerotherapeutics.description: Article 'Aerotherapeutics' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 1), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. The air, however, may be modified in composition or in temperature. Inhalation is the most common and successful method of applying it—when modified in composition—to the human body.

pmc-10636024.creator: Ke Guo, Deshan Zhao
pmc-10636024.description: The purpose of this study was to investigate the correlation between GFR and unit renal volume in infants with congenital hydronephrosis measured by 99mTc-DMSA static renal imaging and ultrasonography. According to the classification of hydronephrosis, 38 infants aged 0–12 months with congenital hydronephrosis were divided into six groups: healthy kidney groups, mild hydronephrosis groups, and severe hydronephrosis groups.

pmc-10701946.title: Evaluation of optimum classification measures used to define textbook outcome among patients undergoing curative-intent resection of gastric cancer
pmc-10701946.creator: L Bobrzynski, K Sędłak, K Rawicz-Pruszyński, P Kolodziejczyk, A Szczepanik, W Polkowski, P Richter, M Sierzega
pmc-10701946.description: BackgroundTextbook outcome (TO) is a composite measure reflecting various aspects of services provided to patients with solid malignancies. We sought to evaluate the importance of various TO components previously proposed for gastric cancer.MethodsProspectively maintained electronic databases of 1,743 patients treated in two academic surgical centres were reviewed.

pmc-10712036.title: The use of foundational ontologies in biomedical research
pmc-10712036.creator: César H Bernabé, Núria Queralt-Rosinach, Vítor E Silva Souza, Luiz Olavo Bonino da Silva Santos, Barend Mons, Annika Jacobsen, Marco Roos
pmc-10712036.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundThe FAIR principles recommend the use of controlled vocabularies, such as ontologies, to define data and metadata concepts. Ontologies are currently modelled following different approaches, sometimes describing conflicting definitions of the same concepts, which can affect interoperability. To cope with that, prior literature suggests organising ontologies in levels, where domain specific (low-level) ontologies are grounded in domain independent high-level ontologies (i.e., foundational ontologies). In this level-based organisation, foundational ontologies work as translators of intended meaning, thus improving interoperability.

pmc-11348553.description: BackgroundBreast milk is the first, highly valuable, and solely natural food recommended for infants in their first six months of life, which is critical for children's overall growth and development. pmc-11607032.title: Adaptive infrared patterns for microscopic surface reconstructions
pmc-11607032.creator: Srdjan Milosavljevic, Zoltan Bardosi, Yusuf Oezbek, Wolfgang Freysinger
pmc-11607032.description: PurposeMulti-zoom microscopic surface reconstructions of operating sites, especially in ENT surgeries, would allow multimodal image fusion for determining the amount of resected tissue, for recognizing critical structures, and novel tools for intraoperative quality assurance. pmc-12609626.description: Simple SummaryYoung animals are fundamental to sustainable animal husbandry, yet the management and feeding strategies for young ruminants face significant challenges, particularly high illness and mortality rates in early development. pmc-12657913.title: Enhanced optical visible light positioning via RSS-based evolutionary optimization under LOS and NLOS conditions

In this article, the Received Signal Strength algorithm (RSS) is used for locating.

pmc-12663954.title: Anisotropic fluorescence emission by diatoms modifies the underwater oceanic light field
pmc-12663954.creator: Joan Salvador Font-Muñoz, Jorge Arrieta, Marc Sourisseau, Idan Tuval, Gotzon Basterretxea
pmc-12663954.description: SignificancePhytoplankton are microscopic organisms that underpin marine food webs and play a central role in global carbon cycling. This study shows that certain diatoms, a major group of phytoplankton, emit chlorophyll fluorescence in a strongly directional manner, influenced by their shape, internal structure, and collective orientation.

pmc-13575845.creator: Rayan Meer
pmc-13575845.description: PurposeSystemic sclerosis is a connective tissue disorder that presents with various orofacial manifestations, which may influence oral health status and complicate dental management.
